title: Generic 80 km G.652.D span loaded in the O- to U-bands: inputs of the band-requirements table (span loss, inter-channel SRS, gain requirement)
model: Coupled power equations of inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering (signals only, no Raman pumps, no ASE, no Kerr effects), integrated numerically with the measured SSMF Raman gain-efficiency profile (tables_bands.py, layer L2 numerical solver)

device.host: ITU-T G.652.D single-mode fiber, suppressed OH peak
device.transition: stimulated Raman scattering between signal channels

reference_plane: span input (all bands launched together after the band combiner) to span output (before the band splitter); band combiner/splitter, gain-flattening filter and connector losses are not included
notes: Abbreviations in 'ref': [P] = B.J. Puttnam et al., High data-rate OESCLU-band transmission, J. Lightwave Technol. 43(23), 10371-10379 (2025), doi:10.1109/JLT.2025.3543448 (author accepted manuscript, Aston eprint 47272, read 17 Nov 2026; journal version of manuscript ref. [7]); [F] = manuscript ref. [14], Ferrari et al., J. Lightwave Technol. 38(16), 4279-4291 (2020) (accepted version read 17 Nov 2026); [Y] = J. Yang et al., On the feasibility of SCL-band transmission over G.654.E-compliant long-haul fibre links, ECOC 2025 (UCL Discovery 10217063, read 17 Nov 2026); [S] = D. Semrau, R.I. Killey, P. Bayvel, The Gaussian noise model in the presence of inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering, J. Lightwave Technol. 36(14), 3046-3055 (2018), arXiv:1801.02460 (arXiv full text read); [GNPy] = Telecom Infra Project, oopt-gnpy, master branch, gnpy/core/parameters.py and gnpy/example-data/eqpt_config.json (read 17 Nov 2026). The launch powers of [P] are applied to fully and uniformly loaded ITU-T bands; this is a stated scenario, not a reproduction of the experiment of [P] (which occupied 37.6 THz between 1281.2 and 1649.9 nm and used six distributed Raman pumps).

att_lambda.applies_to: wavelengths of the measured attenuation anchors (one fiber, the 50/100 km span of [P])

verification.note: accepted manuscript read; confirm in the version of record

att_value.applies_to: attenuation at att_lambda of the G.652.D-class fiber of [P]; used as the attenuation of the generic span

att_model.value: piecewise-linear interpolation in wavelength through (att_lambda, att_value); linear extrapolation with the slope of the end segment below 1300 nm and above 1625 nm
att_model.applies_to: attenuation of every channel bin between 1260 and 1675 nm; values below 1300 nm and above 1625 nm are extrapolations, not data

verification.consistency: interpolated 0.283 and 0.252 dB/km at 1385 and 1425 nm against 0.27 and 0.24 dB/km measured on a different low-water-peak G.652.D fiber [Y]; extrapolated 0.381 dB/km at 1260 nm against '~0.38 dB/km (in O-band)' for the measured G.652.D fiber of [F]; extrapolated 0.225 dB/km at 1675 nm is not backed by data. A shift of all values by -0.03 / +0.03 dB/km changes the band-average ISRS power changes by up to -0.52 / +0.34 dB (C-band; S and U about 0.4-0.5 dB) (tables_bands.py, results 'sensitivity_attenuation')

source.ref: [58] Corning SMF-28 Ultra product information sheet

att_spec_smf28ultra.applies_to: maximum attenuation of one commercial G.652.D fiber, for comparison only (not used in the computation)

verification.note: 1383, 1490 and 1550 nm values as in card RAMAN-G652; 1310 and 1625 nm values from a search-result excerpt of the SMF-28 Ultra 200 sheet (PI1450); the Corning PDF could not be opened automatically (HTTP 403); confirm before printing

att_O_F.applies_to: highest O-band attenuation of the measured G.652.D fiber of [F]; comparison only

att_pump_lwp_Y.applies_to: measured attenuation of a low-water-peak G.652.D fiber (86.2 km span) at Raman pump wavelengths; comparison only

L_span.applies_to: span length of the band-requirements table

P_band_P.applies_to: band-total launch powers; here spread uniformly over each full ITU-T band (flat power spectral density within a band); the 1-3 dB channel-power gradients used in [P] are not modeled

source.locator: Table II (32 GBd, 50 GHz grid; 30 nm around the zero-dispersion wavelength left unused in the O-band)

nch_F.applies_to: channel counts of the full O- to L-band system study of [F]; used only for the alternative loading scenario

Pch_F_75km.applies_to: alternative loading scenario (O- to L-band only); band totals = P_ch + 10 log10(N_ch), spread uniformly over the full ITU-T band

raman_profile.applies_to: Raman gain efficiency of SSMF for the reference pump frequency 206.1846 THz (1454 nm), offsets 0-42 THz; zero beyond 42 THz

verification.note: as recorded in the data-file header (all 90 elements compared with a copy of the repository file downloaded on 17 Nov 2026; 6 of them re-read from the master branch); the measurement behind the GNPy profile is not documented in the repository

f_ref_raman.applies_to: pump frequency for which raman_profile is given

A_ref_raman_gnpy.applies_to: check value only: effective area at 1454 nm of the GNPy SSMF area model

Aeff_1550.applies_to: effective area of the SSMF at 1550 nm used by the area-scaling model

core_radius.applies_to: core radius of the step-index Gaussian-mode model A(f) = pi a^2 / ln V(f) used only to scale A_eff with frequency

n1.applies_to: core index of the area-scaling model

f_ref_area.applies_to: frequency (1550 nm) at which Aeff_1550 applies in the area-scaling model

verification.consistency: with a, n1 and Aeff_1550 the model gives 75.747 um^2 at 1454 nm, equal to A_ref_raman_gnpy within 0.001 % (tables_bands.py check 'area_model')

source.ref: [GNPy] FiberParams.effective_area_overlap; same definition in T. Geisler, B. Palsdottir, Selecting the right NZDF fiber for distributed Raman amplification, OFS white paper (2006)

area_overlap_rule.applies_to: pump-Stokes overlap area entering the Raman gain efficiency

raman_scaling.value: C(f_p -> f_s) = g0(f_p - f_s) * (f_p / f_ref) * A_ov(f_ref - df, f_ref) / A_ov(f_p, f_s); depletion of the higher-frequency wave weighted by f_p / f_s (photon-number conservation)

source.basis: gain term identical to the Fiber.cr method of [GNPy] (normalized_gamma_raman * f_pump / effective_area_overlap); depletion term as in Eq. (11) of the manuscript

raman_scaling.applies_to: Raman gain efficiency between any two signal bins between 1260 and 1675 nm

verification.consistency: variants without area scaling, without any scaling, with the profile truncated at 15 THz and with the triangular profile of [S] are reported in the results file ('profile_variants')

source.locator: Table I(b) (0.4 1/(W km) at 14 THz) and Eq. (10); triangular approximation valid up to approximately 15 THz

Cr_slope_S.applies_to: slope of the linear (triangular) Raman gain approximation, used only for the code check and the comparison with Eq. (10) of [S]

source.basis: C-band load near 20 dBm and C+L load near 23 dBm as in the examples discussed with Eq. (10) of [S]

check_loads.applies_to: contiguous uniform loads used only for the code check (closed form) and for the comparison with Eq. (10)

check_alpha_const.applies_to: wavelength-independent attenuation of the code check only

df_bin.applies_to: width of the frequency bins that represent the uniformly loaded bands

verification.consistency: 0.05 THz bins change every band average and edge value by at most 0.016 dB, 0.2 THz bins by at most 0.032 dB (results 'sensitivity_bin_width')
